name: 3D Half-Gaussian Splatting
definition: A plug-and-play reconstruction kernel that replaces the standard 3D Gaussian in 3D-GS with a 3D Half-Gaussian to address shape and color discontinuities (Gibbs phenomenon) at object boundaries and texture-rich areas, achieving higher rendering quality without compromising speed.
summary: 3D Half-Gaussian Splatting is a reconstruction kernel that replaces standard Gaussians with split halves having different opacities to fix boundary discontinuities while preserving volumetric rendering speed.
